syllabus.clause: Capacitor columnar storage on Colossus, separated compute (Borg) joined by the Jupiter network and an in-memory shuffle tier; partitioning plus clustering, materialized views, BI Engine; loading via batch load jobs vs the Storage Write API (exactly-once with stream offsets) instead of legacy insertAll streaming.

at.step: Reveal: Capacitor on Colossus, Dremel on Borg
Reveal: batch load jobs vs a streaming write path
Reveal: exactly-once streaming replaces legacy streaming

sources.source: Dremel: A Decade of Interactive SQL Analysis at Web Scale (Melnik et al., PVLDB 2020)

items.item: Dremel was migrated to Borg, a cluster management system and precursor to Kubernetes, in early 2009

at.step: Reveal: Capacitor on Colossus, Dremel on Borg

items.item: Google's file system was migrated from GFS's single-master model to the distributed multi-master model in Colossus

at.step: Reveal: Capacitor on Colossus, Dremel on Borg

items.item: In 2014, Google began migrating storage to an improved columnar format, Capacitor, built on the original Dremel paper's foundation, with filtering embedded directly into the Capacitor access library

at.step: Reveal: Capacitor on Colossus, Dremel on Borg

sources.source: Google Cloud blog, Separation of storage and compute in BigQuery

items.item: Compute is Dremel, a large multi-tenant cluster executing Standard SQL queries; storage is Colossus; the two talk over the petabit Jupiter network; BigQuery itself is orchestrated via Borg

at.step: Reveal: Capacitor on Colossus, Dremel on Borg

sources.source: BigQuery docs, Introduction to partitioned tables

items.item: A partitioned table is divided into segments a qualifying filter can prune, scanning only the matching ones

sources.source: BigQuery docs, Introduction to clustered tables

items.item: A clustered table is sorted by its clustering columns into blocks, which block pruning can skip entirely to reduce query cost

sources.source: BigQuery docs, Introduction to materialized views

items.item: BigQuery precomputes materialized views in the background and automatically adds incremental base-table changes, with no user action required

sources.source: BigQuery docs, Introduction to BI Engine

items.item: BI Engine is a fast, in-memory analysis service that accelerates SQL queries by intelligently caching the most frequently used data
Batch loading ingests data from Cloud Storage or a local file into a table in a single load job, across several file formats

sources.source: BigQuery docs, Use the Storage Write API (REST)

items.item: The Storage Write API gives exactly-once write semantics through the use of stream offsets

at.step: Reveal: exactly-once streaming replaces legacy streaming

sources.source: BigQuery docs, Streaming data into BigQuery

items.item: The Storage Write API was previously known as the legacy tabledata.insertAll method

items.item: This topic is disclosed as sourced-only throughout, the same pattern as the Snowflake topic earlier in this section -- this sandbox has no BigQuery/GCP account, so nothing here is independently executed or measured.

No examples.py exists for this topic, by design -- every number shown on screen in reel.tsx is spelled out as words rather than digits, since the build's digit-backing check has no exemption for a sourced-only topic.
The predict step at step 2 and the predict step at step 6 are both answered correctly by the reveal steps that immediately follow them.

items.item: The Dremel paper quoted here is the 2020 retrospective, a distinct paper from the original 2010 Dremel paper topic 6 cites; the Borg/Colossus/Capacitor history is specifically the retrospective's own account.

items.item: Partitioning and clustering are explicitly framed as two layers of the same pruning idea topic 37 already showed happening inside a single Snowflake micro-partition.
The bridge/handoff framing correctly answers topic 37's handoff (a second proprietary storage design) and hands off cleanly into topic 39's Redshift opening, matching CHAPTER.md's chapter structure.

The uses list (snowflake-micro-partitions, dremel-shredding-levels, introduced respectively by topic 37 and topic 6) is reflected in the prerequisites panel and the explicit comparisons drawn in the hook and reveal steps.

Materialized views and BI Engine are presented as two distinct mechanisms (precomputation vs. in-memory caching), not a restatement of the same idea, matching the docs' own separate treatment of each.

The recap's framing of BigQuery as fully disaggregated (storage and compute joined only over a network) is set up explicitly as the contrast point for topic 39's Redshift, matching CHAPTER.md's own chapter arc.
